task: Audit the non-dot, non-venv repository and produce a phased, lossless cleanup and restructuring plan rooted at START_HERE.md without implementing the cleanup
instructions: Replace every pending status with apply plus decision and evidence, or skip plus reason. Keep names and structure unchanged.

methods.name: diagnosing-bugs
methods.reason: The task is a forward-looking repository audit and plan, not a reported failure or performance regression.

methods.name: domain-modeling
methods.decision: Define lossless, authority, liveness, current state, chronology, recovery, and protected scope precisely before the self-grilling decisions enter the plan.
methods.evidence: The user authorized the grilling session, and the cleanup depends on stable meanings for the file-liveness registry and the three-document authority lifecycle.

methods.name: how
methods.decision: Trace entry points, runtime flows, ownership, and dependencies before judging code or files obsolete.
methods.evidence: .agents/skills/how/SKILL.md and the user's request to understand the codebase before restructuring it

methods.name: why
methods.reason: The task needs current liveness and dependency evidence, not a sourced reconstruction of one past design decision.

methods.name: architect
methods.reason: Plan-flow stops before code crosses function or module interfaces; codebase-design owns the current structural analysis.

methods.name: arena
methods.reason: No competing implementation artifacts will be built during this read-only planning route.

methods.name: codebase-design
methods.decision: Judge modules by depth, locality, seam placement, test surface, and the deletion test while producing cleanup candidates.

methods.name: tdd
methods.reason: No production behavior is implemented in plan-flow.

methods.name: pocock-tdd
methods.reason: The deliverable is a plan; each implementation phase will name behavior-level verification without running a TDD loop now.

methods.name: implement
methods.reason: The selected plan-flow route explicitly stops before implementation.

methods.name: code-review
methods.reason: There is no production diff to review; the planning gates inspect the plan artifact instead.

pstack_principles.name: principle-boundary-discipline
pstack_principles.decision: Preserve true CLI, filesystem, data, and external-system seams; remove internal validation or adapters only after callers and tests prove them redundant.
pstack_principles.evidence: The requested cleanup spans tools, data artifacts, workflow hooks, and trading code with distinct system seams.

pstack_principles.name: principle-build-the-lever
pstack_principles.reason: The plan will specify a cleanup manifest and verifier, but building those implementation artifacts now would violate plan-flow.

pstack_principles.name: principle-encode-lessons-in-structure
pstack_principles.decision: Replace repeated operational prose with discoverable config, generated indexes, or checks; retain judgment-heavy decisions in one durable source.
pstack_principles.evidence: START_HERE.md repeats commands and workflow policy that also exist in scripts, hooks, and AGENTS.md.

pstack_principles.name: principle-exhaust-the-design-space
pstack_principles.decision: Compare at least three target repository shapes before selecting the phased migration.
pstack_principles.evidence: The whole-repository restructure has no single obvious file layout and plan-flow requires alternatives.

pstack_principles.name: principle-experience-first
pstack_principles.decision: Optimize the entry path for the next agent and maintainer so START_HERE.md answers where to begin without caching discoverable facts.
pstack_principles.evidence: The user explicitly named START_HERE.md as the universal entry point.

pstack_principles.name: principle-fix-root-causes
pstack_principles.reason: No defect is being debugged; obsolete-file judgments will use dependency and history evidence instead.

pstack_principles.name: principle-foundational-thinking
pstack_principles.decision: Define the file-liveness classification and target information hierarchy before planning moves or deletions.
pstack_principles.evidence: Lossless cleanup depends on distinguishing authoritative, generated, reproducible, historical, and dead material.

pstack_principles.name: principle-guard-the-context-window
pstack_principles.decision: Partition exploration by code, documentation, and data or operations, and retain only file pointers and findings in the main thread.
pstack_principles.evidence: The repository has enough files and long documents to overwhelm one undifferentiated scan.

pstack_principles.name: principle-laziness-protocol
pstack_principles.decision: Prefer deletion, consolidation, and flatter ownership over new layers or replacement documentation.
pstack_principles.evidence: The user's desired end state is an extremely lean repository with no functionality loss.

pstack_principles.name: principle-make-operations-idempotent
pstack_principles.decision: Require the eventual inventory, move, archive, and delete operations to be dry-runnable and safe after partial completion.
pstack_principles.evidence: A whole-repository cleanup can be interrupted and must converge without duplicating or losing files.

pstack_principles.name: principle-migrate-callers-then-delete-legacy-apis
pstack_principles.decision: Move imports, command references, documentation pointers, and tests in the same phase that removes each old path.
pstack_principles.evidence: The user wants the old code gone, and internal callers do not justify compatibility layers.

pstack_principles.name: principle-minimize-reader-load
pstack_principles.decision: Measure cleanup candidates by layers to trace and hidden state to remember, then collapse one-caller wrappers and duplicate knowledge.
pstack_principles.evidence: START_HERE.md currently asks a newcomer to cross several documents and retain historical state before acting.

pstack_principles.name: principle-model-the-domain
pstack_principles.decision: Represent the audit as a file-liveness registry with ownership, authority, reproducibility, consumers, replacement, and disposition fields.
pstack_principles.evidence: Scattered keep or delete judgments would otherwise repeat shape assumptions across hundreds of files.

pstack_principles.name: principle-never-block-on-the-human
pstack_principles.decision: Infer reversible planning choices from repository evidence and surface any real product decision in the completed plan instead of pausing the audit.
pstack_principles.evidence: The user supplied the target, exclusions, and lossless constraint; the remaining work is observable.

pstack_principles.name: principle-outcome-oriented-execution
pstack_principles.decision: Plan explicit verification points that converge on the target tree without permanent redirect files or dual documentation systems.
pstack_principles.evidence: The requested end state is one clear entry path and a lean tree, not a long compatibility period.

pstack_principles.name: principle-prove-it-works
pstack_principles.decision: Every proposed deletion class needs direct proof from imports, invocations, tests, artifacts, or reproducibility before removal; the final tree needs full checks and smoke runs.
pstack_principles.evidence: The user made losslessness the acceptance condition.

pstack_principles.name: principle-redesign-from-first-principles
pstack_principles.decision: Design the target repository as if START_HERE.md, durable memory, and the live trading workflow had been foundational, then migrate toward it in checked phases.
pstack_principles.evidence: The user requested an entire repository restructure rather than local tidying.

pstack_principles.name: principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state
pstack_principles.reason: Explorers are read-only and the implementation plan will sequence repository writes; no concurrent mutable target is required.

pstack_principles.name: principle-sequence-verifiable-units
pstack_principles.decision: Split the cleanup into inventory, retirement, code consolidation, layout migration, documentation compression, and final proof units, each ending in checks.
pstack_principles.evidence: A repository-wide migration cannot be verified honestly as one batch.

pstack_principles.name: principle-subtract-before-you-add
pstack_principles.decision: Retire dead and reproducible material before introducing the final directory structure or rewriting the remaining documentation.
pstack_principles.evidence: The user asked to remove useless code and files before polishing the surviving tree.

pstack_principles.name: principle-type-system-discipline
pstack_principles.reason: The planning route defines no production signatures or typed data model; implementation phases will apply this when consolidating typed code.

supplemental_principles.name: pocock-codebase-glossary
supplemental_principles.decision: Use module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage, and locality consistently in every architectural finding.

supplemental_principles.name: pocock-codebase-depth
supplemental_principles.decision: Use the deletion test to distinguish shallow pass-through modules from deep modules that concentrate knowledge.

supplemental_principles.name: pocock-codebase-principles
supplemental_principles.decision: Keep interfaces small, treat them as test surfaces, and reject hypothetical seams that have only one adapter.

supplemental_principles.name: pocock-codebase-testability
supplemental_principles.decision: Prefer modules whose dependencies enter through parameters and whose observable results can be checked without internal mutation.

supplemental_principles.name: pocock-codebase-relationships
supplemental_principles.decision: Evaluate every proposed seam by the module interface it hosts, the adapters it needs, and the locality and leverage it creates.

supplemental_principles.name: pocock-codebase-rejected-framings
supplemental_principles.decision: Do not score modules by line-count ratios or confuse interfaces with language-level signatures.

supplemental_principles.name: pocock-codebase-going-deeper
supplemental_principles.decision: Classify dependencies before recommending that shallow modules merge or move behind a smaller interface.

supplemental_principles.name: pocock-deepening-dependencies
supplemental_principles.decision: Tag each candidate dependency as in-process, local-substitutable, remote-owned, or external so its test plan is honest.

supplemental_principles.name: pocock-deepening-seams
supplemental_principles.decision: Keep internal test seams private and expose a new port only when production and test adapters make the seam real.

supplemental_principles.name: pocock-deepening-tests
supplemental_principles.decision: Replace tests of retired shallow modules with observable tests at the surviving deep module's interface.

supplemental_principles.name: pocock-design-it-twice
supplemental_principles.reason: No specific deepened module interface has been selected; the plan compares repository layouts without inventing production interfaces.

supplemental_principles.name: pocock-tdd-good-tests
supplemental_principles.reason: No tests are written during plan-flow.

supplemental_principles.name: pocock-tdd-seams
supplemental_principles.reason: Codebase-design supplies the test-surface decision needed by the plan; no TDD seam is exercised now.

supplemental_principles.name: pocock-tdd-antipatterns
supplemental_principles.reason: No production test suite changes occur in this planning task.

supplemental_principles.name: pocock-tdd-loop
supplemental_principles.reason: The red-green-refactor loop belongs to the later implementation route.

supplemental_principles.name: pocock-test-quality
supplemental_principles.decision: Specify checks against public behavior and real entry points so tests survive internal consolidation.
supplemental_principles.evidence: The lossless requirement cannot be proven by path-existence checks alone.

supplemental_principles.name: pocock-mocking-boundaries
supplemental_principles.reason: The plan does not create a new third-party dependency or test double.

supplemental_principles.name: pocock-writing-context
supplemental_principles.decision: Make START_HERE.md a strong pointer to live state and durable memory rather than an always-loaded copy of them.
supplemental_principles.evidence: The user wants START_HERE.md to remain the universal entry document.

supplemental_principles.name: pocock-writing-loads
supplemental_principles.decision: Spend context load only on universal rules and spend human lookup effort on branch-specific history or evidence.

supplemental_principles.name: pocock-writing-hierarchy
supplemental_principles.decision: Put immediate session steps in START_HERE.md, current state in one disclosed file, and durable chronology in MEMORY.md.

supplemental_principles.name: pocock-writing-completion
supplemental_principles.decision: Give every cleanup phase an observable finish condition and refuse vague outcomes such as documentation cleaned up.

supplemental_principles.name: pocock-writing-split
supplemental_principles.decision: Split the plan by independently verifiable migration phase while keeping the final repository documentation split to the fewest live branches.
supplemental_principles.evidence: The implementation spans more than three phases, while the target documentation budget is one or two files beyond memory.

supplemental_principles.name: pocock-writing-leading-words
supplemental_principles.decision: Use stable classification terms such as authoritative, generated, reproducible, historical, and dead throughout the plan and later manifest.

supplemental_principles.name: pocock-writing-pruning
supplemental_principles.decision: Delete duplicate caches of config and commands, disclose branch-only history, and retain one source for each decision.
supplemental_principles.evidence: The user's complaint is documentation sediment and repeated obsolete material.

supplemental_principles.name: pocock-implementation-checks
supplemental_principles.reason: Implementation checks will be specified per phase but no implementation step runs in plan-flow.

supplemental_principles.name: akita-code-style
supplemental_principles.decision: Require surviving and consolidated production functions, names, types, and modules to meet the repository's Akita limits.
supplemental_principles.evidence: AGENTS.md Code style block and the user's request to clean useless code as well as files

supplemental_principles.name: akita-comments
supplemental_principles.decision: Preserve comments that carry why or provenance and remove only narration that the code already states.
supplemental_principles.evidence: AGENTS.md Comments block makes comment intent part of losslessness.

supplemental_principles.name: akita-tests
supplemental_principles.decision: Require regression tests for consolidation and one project command for each independently shippable phase.
supplemental_principles.evidence: AGENTS.md Tests block and the user's no-functionality-loss requirement

supplemental_principles.name: akita-dependencies
supplemental_principles.decision: Preserve dependency injection and project-owned adapters while removing unused third-party packages only after import and runtime proof.

supplemental_principles.name: akita-structure
supplemental_principles.decision: Organize surviving files by one responsibility and predictable framework or domain paths, with files below 500 lines.
supplemental_principles.evidence: AGENTS.md Structure block and the requested whole-repository restructure

supplemental_principles.name: akita-formatting
supplemental_principles.decision: Run each language's default formatter after code moves and consolidation instead of hand-formatting.

supplemental_principles.name: akita-logging
supplemental_principles.decision: Keep structured logs for diagnostics and plain text for user-facing commands when consolidating tools.

foundations.name: codebase-design
foundations.decision: Use deep-module vocabulary and the deletion test as the foundation for all restructuring candidates.

foundations.name: diagnosing-bugs
foundations.reason: Repository cleanup planning is not a bug diagnosis.

foundations.name: domain-modeling
foundations.reason: Existing glossary terms will be consumed; plan-flow will not create or edit domain glossary or ADR files.
